content.title: About
content.content: Potato hash brown with cheese is made from fresh potatoes grated coarsely, mixed with shredded cheese, spices and a small amount of flour. The mixture is shaped into small patties and fried until golden and crisp. It is a hearty, flavorful snack popular in fast‑food and home cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Hash brown originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a way to use leftover potatoes.
Adding cheese gives the patty a richer, umami flavor and a softer interior.
Traditionally hash browns are served with sour cream or ketchup.
In some regions they are called "potato pancakes" or "potato croquettes".
A vegetarian version without meat but with cheese fits most diets.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Fresh potatoes contain vitamin C, which helps strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Protein from cheese
items.content: Shredded cheese adds complete protein and calcium important for bone health.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Hash browns provide quick energy from carbohydrates.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Potato skin and a small amount of flour supply fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Frying in oil increases calories and saturated fat levels.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or dairy allergies.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Cheese is often salty, making the dish high in sodium, which may be unsuitable for hypertension.

items.title: Oil degradation at high heat
items.content: Overheating oil can create harmful compounds; it is recommended to fry at medium temperature.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a standalone snack, as a side to salads, or inside burgers. Sprinkle with fresh herbs, add sour cream, yogurt sauce, or a spicy dip to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked hash browns in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a single layer on a tray, then transfer to a freezer bag – they keep well for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven to restore crispness.
